concepts.name: Woodland Retreat
concepts.tagline: A single 40-foot room in the trees, with the porch turned to the view.
concepts.description: One 40-foot high-cube container holds a sleeping room, bath, kitchen and living space. A generous screened porch and a small deck extend the living area into the forest. The long side faces the view; the entry and path stay behind.

zones.name: Sleeping
zones.accessibility: A 1.5 m turning circle does not fit with the double bed; an accessible variant needs a longer room or smaller bed.

zones.name: Bathroom
zones.accessibility: 2.1 m clear length; a 1.5 m turning circle needs a layout review.

zones.name: Kitchen
zones.accessibility: 1.6 m clear in front of the counter; provide a lowered work section.

zones.name: Living
zones.accessibility: Sliding door to the screened porch; 0.9 m clear route.

porches.note: Screened outdoor room facing the view.

foundation.note: Type, depth, frost and rock need geotechnical review.

features.outdoor: 4.4 × 3.05 m screened porch plus 1.2 m deck
features.solar: Solar array on the main roof
features.green_roof: Not included; can be tested as an option
features.accessibility: Step-free porch route is intended; bathroom and sleeping turning space need redesign.
features.environment: Small footprint, external insulation and a replaceable rainscreen.

materials.disclosure: Continuous external insulation reduces thermal bridging. Thickness and moisture performance need hygrothermal review.

materials.disclosure: Replaceable, repairable, but needs durable species, ventilation and fire review.

concepts.name: Micro Studio
concepts.tagline: Twenty feet of shelter, with most of the living outdoors.
concepts.description: A 20-foot container holds a compact bath, kitchenette and sleeping/living room. The screened porch and deck are almost as large as the interior, making the outdoors part of the home.

zones.name: Bathroom
zones.accessibility: Compact wet room; turning space is tight.

zones.name: Kitchenette
zones.accessibility: One counter run with a bar sink.

zones.name: Sleeping and living
zones.accessibility: A sofa bed or Murphy bed keeps the room flexible.

features.outdoor: 3.2 × 2.4 m screened porch plus 1.6 m deck
features.accessibility: Too small for a 1.5 m turning circle; a seasonal studio, not an accessible permanent home.
features.environment: Smallest footprint and material use; the deck reduces pressure on the interior.

concepts.name: Lakeside Hideaway
concepts.tagline: A protected veranda on the weather side, with a biosolar roof.
concepts.description: A 40-foot container turned so its long side faces the lake, with a deep screened veranda, a biosolar roof and living space opened to the water. The veranda gives shade in summer and a sheltered edge in shoulder seasons.

zones.name: Sleeping
zones.accessibility: Lake-facing window; turning space needs an accessible variant.

porches.note: Deep protected veranda facing the lake.

foundation.note: Placeholder; rock and shoreline review required.

features.outdoor: 6.0 × 3.0 m screened veranda plus 1.0 m deck
features.solar: Raised PV above an extensive green roof
features.green_roof: Biosolar concept; saturated weight and drainage need engineering
features.accessibility: Step-free veranda intended; bathroom is compact.
features.environment: Shading from the veranda and a green roof; lake edge must remain undisturbed.

concepts.name: Forest Courtyard

concepts.description: Two 40-foot containers face each other across a timber-framed connecting space. The link creates a sheltered courtyard for meals and work, with sleeping in one module and living in the other.

porches.note: Covered outdoor seating outside the link.

features.accessibility: Courtyard route can be step-free; the bathroom remains compact.
features.environment: Two modules share a courtyard instead of extending the building footprint.

concepts.name: L-Shaped Haven
concepts.tagline: Two containers form a sheltered corner without a single long road.
concepts.description: One horizontal container holds living and cooking; a second, rotated container holds sleeping and work. The L wraps a sheltered porch and deck, leaving the view open to the south and east.

porches.note: Screened porch in the sheltered corner.

foundation.note: Two independent foundations; frost and rock review required.

features.outdoor: 4.4 × 2.8 m screened porch plus 1.2 m deck
features.accessibility: Step-free porch; sleeping and bath need accessible variants.
features.environment: The L protects the porch from wind and leaves the forest view open.

concepts.name: Open Plan
concepts.tagline: Two adjacent containers become one wider home.
concepts.description: Two 40-foot containers sit side by side, with a large structural opening between them to create a wider living space. Sleeping, bath and work occupy the quieter side.

structure.notes: Large opening between adjacent modules needs engineered framing and transfer beams.

zones.name: Living
zones.accessibility: Wide living space across both modules.

structure.notes: Large opening between adjacent modules needs engineered framing and transfer beams.

foundation.note: Adjacent modules need a shared foundation strategy.

features.outdoor: 4.5 × 3.0 m screened porch plus 1.2 m deck
features.accessibility: Wider interior helps circulation, but the bathroom still needs an accessible layout.
features.environment: Reuses two shells and avoids a larger footprint, but the wall removal is structurally significant.
